## What has happened to measles elimination in the Americas?

### 1. Has the Americas lost its measles elimination status?

Yes, the Region of the Americas lost its verification as free from endemic measles transmission in November 2025, following the re-establishment of endemic transmission in Canada.

The decision was announced by PAHO on 10 November 2025, following a review by the independent Measles and Rubella Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission (RVC). The Commission concluded that the same measles virus genotype and lineage had circulated uninterrupted in Canada for at least 12 months.

The Americas first eliminated measles in 2016 and regained its regional elimination status in 2024. It was the first and remains the only WHO region to have achieved regional measles elimination, and the only one to have achieved it twice.

# Can the U.S. regain its measles elimination status? Here's what to know
[Health](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/health)  Nov 17, 2026 4:44 PM EST
The U.S. has lost its measles-elimination status for the first time in 26 years, an international health organization determined Tuesday.
With more than 5,400 cases and six deaths reported in 2026 so far, the status loss is an indication that measles spread in the U.S. is now considered endemic.
When measles is considered "eliminated" in a country, that doesn't mean there are zero measles cases. It measures whether there are large outbreaks or continuous transmission for 12 months or more. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has reported 43 outbreaks, which it defines as three or more related cases, this year.

Measles in the U.S. was first declared eliminated in 2000 by an independent commission of experts from the Pan American Health Organization, PAHO, when the country recorded 85 cases.

PAHO met from Nov. 10 to 13 to vote on the United States' and other countries' statuses. Bolivia and Mexico also lost their measles elimination status on Tuesday.

The loss of the elimination status for the U.S. doesn't come as a surprise. Measles cases have been rising since 2025 as vaccination rates among kindergarteners have dropped while non-medical vaccine exemptions have risen.

CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz [said in a statement Tuesday](https://www.cdc.gov/media/releases/2026/loss-of-usmeasles-elimination-status.html) that "the measles elimination designation is not what protects Americans. Vaccination does."

The U.S. can regain its elimination status once it is able to prove that it can contain outbreaks and the virus isn't circulating in the population.
Brazil, for example, lost its status in 2019 before regaining it in 2024 "following extensive vaccination, surveillance and outbreak response efforts," according to PAHO.

The call follows the 10–13 November meeting of the Measles, Rubella and Congenital Rubella Syndrome Elimination Regional Monitoring and Re-Verification Commission (RVC), which reviewed the latest epidemiological situation across the Region. Following the Commission’s assessment and recommendations, which were accepted by PAHO Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa, endemic measles transmission was determined to have been re-established in Bolivia, Mexico, and the United States. All three countries have therefore lost their measles elimination status.

The Region of the Americas, the first in the world to eliminate measles, regained its elimination status in 2024 after successfully interrupting endemic transmission in Venezuela and Brazil. However, the loss of regional status in November 2025, following sustained transmission in Canada, was a major setback. The subsequent loss of elimination status by Bolivia, Mexico and the United States marks a further deterioration in the regional situation and makes the path towards restoring elimination more challenging.

***Updated Nov. 24, 2026***
